name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *all* PRs for two weeks. This lets us measure real impact without risking broken workflows—trade-off is temporary noise in contributor experience. After the test, we’ll decide whether to roll it out fully based on data, not assumptions.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow mode won’t catch PR-Agent’s worst flaw: false negatives. It normalizes broken PRs by hiding them from contributors, teaching teams to ignore critical gaps. Instead, run a controlled A/B test: apply PR-Agent only to non-blocking PRs for two weeks, then compare false negative rates against a control group—if the gap widens, the tool fails its core purpose.

name: Overhaul
text: Run the A/B test only on PRs from *new contributors*—they’re less likely to have established review patterns and will show clearer false-negative signals. This shrinks the sample size needed to detect meaningful differences, cutting the test duration by half.

name: Sprocket
text: Run the A/B test on new contributors only. False negatives hurt most when reviewers miss critical gaps in unfamiliar code—new contributors amplify that risk. The trade-off is slower feedback for them, but we’ll measure real impact faster. After two weeks, we’ll know if PR-Agent’s false negatives outweigh its benefits.
